atoms.text: The red squirrel is a species of squirrel that lives throughout Europe and Asia. Their red coats act as camouflage, allowing the squirrels to blend in naturally with the bark of pine trees. A red squirrel’s coat changes colour depending on the time of year, ranging from a bright, deep red in the summer to black in the winter, with noticeably larger ear tufts.

Red squirrels are very resourceful creatures, and are good at making use of their environments. Using just twigs, they can make domed dreys about 25 to 30 cm long! The red squirrel’s favourite food is hazelnuts, although they also eat a variety of other nuts, seeds, berries and fungi. When they have too much food, red squirrels will store the food, either in the ground or in little nooks in trees, so they can come back to it later.

atoms.text: Unfortunately, red squirrels are endangered. This means that we have to protect them so that they don’t go extinct. Extinction can happen for a lot of reasons. Red squirrels have become endangered since humans introduced other species into the red squirrel’s habitats. But don’t worry, there are people who are watching the numbers and are working to protect these amazing animals!
